fullPassage: We like to put people into categories. Categories are simple and safe — black or white, good or evil. They save us the effort of looking beyond our own biases to become genuinely curious about someone else. But categories can sabotage our efforts to understand people, by reducing them to two-dimensional stereotypes. While it's easy to assume that the person who dings your car and drives off is an awful person, the truth is there's probably a lot more to it. Similarly, if someone you love or admire is accused of doing something hurtful, you might jump to their defense. "Oh, they didn't mean it," you might say. "They just made a mistake." Some would prefer to be willfully blind to the fact that a good or kind person did a bad thing if it allows them to sustain an uncomplicated way of viewing the world. We would rather judge people by who we believe them to be rather than by their actions. Conversely, we like to imagine that one bad action can determine a person's overall character or humanity. It doesn't.

questions.passage: Categories are simple and safe — black or white, good or evil. They save us the effort of __________ (look) beyond our own biases to become genuinely curious about someone else.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 'the effort of ___'에서 전치사 of 뒤이므로 동사 look은 동명사 looking으로 바꿔야 한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: someone이 비난을 '받는' 대상이므로 「be동사 + 과거분사」 수동태가 되어야 한다. is accused of ~.
det.analysis: someone ... is __________ of doing → 「be + 과거분사」 수동태 (~로 비난받다) → accuse를 과거분사 accused로

questions.passage: We like to put people into categories. Categories are simple and safe — black or white, good or evil. They save us the effort of looking beyond our own biases to become genuinely curious about someone else. But categories can sabotage our efforts to understand people, by reducing them to two-dimensional stereotypes. While it's easy to assume that the person who dings your car and drives off is an awful person, the truth is there's probably __________. Similarly, if someone you love or admire is accused of doing something hurtful, you might jump to their defense. "Oh, they didn't mean it," you might say. "They just made a mistake." Some would prefer to be willfully blind to the fact that a good or kind person did a bad thing if it allows them to sustain an uncomplicated way of viewing the world. We would rather judge people by who we believe them to be rather than by their actions. Conversely, we like to imagine that one bad action can determine a person's overall character or humanity. It doesn't.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 차를 긁고 도망간 사람을 형편없다고 단정하기 쉽지만, '사실은 그 이면에 더 많은 사정이 있을(a lot more to it)' 것이라는 대비 구조이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① a lot more to it — 그 이면에 더 많은 사정이 있다 ←정답 (섣부른 단정에 대한 반전)
❌ ② nothing more to know — 더 알 것이 없다 (문맥 반대)
❌ ③ no one to blame — 탓할 사람이 없다 (문맥 무관)
❌ ④ little time to lose — 지체할 시간이 없다 (문맥 무관)
det.tip: easy to assume ... but the truth is there's probably a lot more to it (단정 vs 실제)
